Per colophon, finished on 1 January 1468 (n.s.).  The flyleaves and pastedowns are from a 15th century Italian noted choirbook.

source_title: Brochure No. 14. Timeless Treasures: A Selection of Illuminated Manuscripts, Miniatures and Early Printed Books
other_info: Incomplete. Border decoration, one illumination with bas-de-page. Final part of Common of Saints. First volume of an original set of three. 30 companion leaves in La Spezia (Museo Civico Amadeo Lia), Venice (Fondazione G. Cini), and some private collections. Four different illuminators worked on the three volumes, each with a distinct artistic background, but two of them embellished this codex: the first is like Maestro Daddesco and Pacino da Bonaguida, seen on ff. 242, and 253. The second artist, more progressive, illuminated ff. 254, 258, 303, and 315, featuring richly embroidered hems, set with precious jewels and clasps, pearls and gems, similar to the style of the Master of the Dominican Effigies.

titles: Books of Hours, Use of Rome and the Carmelites (?), in Latin
artists: Mariano, del Buono di Jacopo, 1433-1504
manuscript_binding: Sewn on five cords, with endbands; bound in early 19th-c. English (?) brown leather over pasteboards, with onlays of red leather dotted in gilt; spine in seven compartments without bands; marbled endpapers conjoint with pastedowns; gilt edges [cat. pl. 1]
other_info:
[See cat. for additional notes, description, and bibliography.] Formerly MS. Lat. liturg. e. 28. i (paper) + 196 + ii (paper). Modern foliation in pencil i, 1-41a, 41b-197. 23 quires mostly of 10, but with numerous leaves missing. Ruled in pale grey-blue ink (quires I-VIII, XIV-XX) and pale brown (remainder). Headed in red; guides to rubrics and colored initials in tiny cursive script; capitals touched in pale yellow wash. | Contents. Hours of the Virgin, Use of Rome (imperfect); Long Hours of the Cross (misbound and imperfect); Penitential Psalms (imperfect); Litany and collects; Office of the Dead, Carmelite (?) use (imperfect); Calendar, very sparse. | Decoration. Four seven-line historiated initials, each below a colored panel with the heading of the text, mostly in square capitals of the humanist style, surrounded by a four-sided border containing further scenes in panels framed in gold. 1r Hours of the Virgin, initial D[omine]: Virgin and Child, lower border with two putti flanking a coat of arms. 81r Hours of the Cross, initial D[omine]: Man of Sorrows, standing in the tomb; 109r Penitential Psalms, initial D[omine]: King David playing the psaltery [cat. pl. 23]; 130r Office of the Dead, initial D[ilexi]: half-length skeleton holding scythe, border in a different style from others with lush acanthus foliage. Four-line painted foliate initials with burnished and painted gold at the start of each hour from Prime to Compline in the Hours of the Virgin; similar three-line initials in to the same hours in the Hours of the Cross; three-line initials in gold with blue, or blue with red, respectively, to Lauds of the Hours of the Virgin and the Cross; two-line initials to psalms, lessons, KL monograms in the calendar, etc.; one-line initials alternately in gold or blue to verses and other minor textual divisions. Illumination attributed by Garzelli to Mariano del Buono di Jacopo. | Made for a member of the Florentine Bellacci family (?): their (?) coat of arms on 1r, vert, a bend argent, with three uncertain five-pointed objects gules, the shield within a wreath held by two putti; matches the Bellacci arms if the five-pointed objects represent cinquefoils or roses. The responses of the nine lessons of the Office of the Dead are assigned by Ottosen to a wide variety of places, mostly French, but also to Sarum and Carmelite uses; the latter is assigned here on acccount of the Bellacci family's Carmelite links. Subsequent provenance includes Adolphe Labitte, Paris bookseller; perhaps bought by Thomas Buchanan with MS Buchanan e. 5 and Buchanan e. 136 in October 1857.
